QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_8

question.text: In an open-ended mutual fund scheme, units can be purchased and redeemed:

answer.text: On any business day at the applicable NAV
Only during the New Fund Offer (NFO) period
Only on the stock exchange where the fund is listed
Only at specified intervals as declared by the AMC

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes open-ended schemes as those that allow investors to enter and exit after the NFO, with units redeemed back to the scheme at the applicable NAV on any business day. There is no fixed maturity period, and the AMC stands ready to issue and repurchase units at the prevailing NAV. The Trap: Option B describes a close-ended fund, where units are offered only during the NFO and the scheme has a fixed maturity. Option C describes the exchange-traded route used by ETFs and the listing route for close-ended schemes, not the standard open-ended transaction with the AMC. Option D describes an interval fund, which allows transactions only during specified intervals. Note: Source page 45 supports the open-ended business-day transaction at applicable NAV, and page 46 supports the interval-fund contrast.
